THE UNIVERSITY OF BAMENDA
College of Technology  ·  Department of Computer Engineering
A real-time agentic AI system for web threat detection and user protection

Supervisor: Prof. Onabid Mathias Akong, Associate Professor
Master's in Computer Engineering — Information Technology and Cyber Security  ·  June 2026
Why web-threat detection needs more than one model

THE BROWSER IS THE ATTACK SURFACE
Phishing, drive-by downloads, credential theft and malicious ads, as the boundary moved from firewall to browser (Provos et al., 2007; Khonji et al., 2013).

SIGNATURES FALL BEHIND
Fast-changing domains, hidden payloads and short-lived infrastructure defeat signature-based tools.

DETECTION GREW SMARTER
Machine learning, then deep learning and Transformers that read URLs in context (Devlin et al., 2019).

FROM ONE MODEL TO AGENTS
Specialised agents for detection, extraction, analysis and reporting, reasoning step by step like analysts (Yao et al., 2023).
Three persistent problems limit AI threat detection for ordinary users and small teams
How can URL analysis be divided among different AI agents, and what is the smallest set of agents needed for a reliable threat assessment?
How can URL classification, behavioural analysis, IOC extraction, MITRE ATT&CK mapping and threat-intelligence lookup be combined into one consistent, accurate system?
What method can combine the agents' results to reduce false alarms while still identifying serious threats when strong evidence is available?
How can historical browsing information improve detection, identify recurring malicious activity and strengthen protection over time?
Thesis Chapter 2 (§2.2–2.9); full references on the final slide
From rules to learning to cooperating agents
Five gaps between research ideas and working systems

FEW COMPLETE MULTI-AGENT SECURITY SYSTEMS
Frameworks show the idea; few open systems apply it end to end.

MODEL AND SERVICE FAILURE
Systems rarely say when a model or service did not answer.

ACCURACY OVER REAL FALSE ALARMS
Lab scores hide how often safe sites are flagged (Sommer & Paxson, 2010).

HISTORICAL CONTEXT UNUSED
Past observations are rarely reused later (Park et al., 2023).

HARD TO REPRODUCE
Private data, closed systems, costly infrastructure.
Four layers with a clear data flow
A three-stage directed acyclic graph, then a Reporter
